title: Memory and V8 GC interview drills

items.question: Explain V8 generational garbage collection in two sentences.
items.answer: Most objects die young in the nursery — Scavenge collects frequently and cheaply. Survivors promote to old space where mark-sweep-compact runs less often but may pause the main thread longer. Generational hypothesis: if it survived once, it will live longer.
followUps: How does this differ from CLR gen2?
items.sixtySeconds: Young Scavenge fast. Old mark-compact slower. Promotion after survival. Main thread pauses in V8.

items.question: A SPA leaks memory after route changes. How do you find the cause?
items.answer: Chrome DevTools Memory: heap snapshot before navigation, snapshot after, compare. Look for Detached DOM nodes, listeners count, retained size on closures. Check removeEventListener on teardown, clear timers, null large captures. Allocation sampling if leak is gradual.
followUps: What is a detached DOM node?
items.sixtySeconds: Snapshot diff. Detached DOM. Listener leak. Closure over big object. cancel timers on unmount.

items.question: Why should Redis client be a singleton in Node, not per request?
items.answer: Per-request createClient allocates connections and wrappers — Scavenge churn and promotion pressure. May hit maxclients. Singleton lives in old space by design — one connection pool shared. Same pattern as HttpClient in C#.
items.sixtySeconds: Singleton pool intentional long-lived root. Per-request churn and connection storm. IHttpClientFactory pattern in C#.

items.question: How do closures cause memory leaks?
items.answer: Inner function reachable from listener/timer keeps entire outer environment alive — including large variables even if inner only uses one field. Fix: capture IDs not graphs, remove listener, use WeakMap for DOM metadata.
items.sixtySeconds: Listener holds closure holds outer vars. Pass id not 5MB JSON. removeEventListener. WeakMap side table.

items.question: Compare V8 GC pauses to CLR server GC.
items.answer: V8 runs GC on main JS thread — major GC can freeze event loop milliseconds. CLR server GC uses background threads for much collection work — less impact on request threads in ASP.NET. Both generational. JS has no IDisposable for memory — only stop referencing.
items.sixtySeconds: V8 pauses main thread. CLR server GC background. Both generational. JS no manual free.

items.question: Does delete operator free memory immediately?
items.answer: No. delete removes a property making object unreachable if no other references — GC reclaims later nondeterministically. For resources like sockets, call close/destroy explicitly. delete is not C++ free.
items.sixtySeconds: delete unlinks property. GC async later. Close sockets explicitly. WeakMap keys are objects.
